newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Four dead in Albania ammo dump blast.
newsitem.headline: Four dead in Albania ammo dump blast.

text.p: An ammunition dump in southern Albania was rocked by explosions on Thursday, killing four people and injuring 14, military officials and doctors said.
Between 10 to 15 people were still trapped inside the dump, said an Italian spokesman for the multinational force which is in the country protecting aid supplies.
Ammunition stores all over Albania were looted during rioting and lawlessness which swept the country in February and March after thousands lost life savings in pyramid investment schemes.
Romanian troops from the international force sped to the scene of Thursday's blast with an ambulance and two trucks and were busy cordoning off the area with Albanian soldiers.
"We do not know what caused the explosion," the spokesman said.
Two weeks ago a dump exploded in northern Albania, killing 27 people, 12 of them children. They had triggered the explosion as they looted the underground store.
Officials spoke of a "big, dynamite explosion" in tunnels and depots on the surface of the dump, in Picar, some 18 km (10 miles) north of Gjirokaster, Albania's southernmost town.
Gjirokaster hospital director Hodo Cela said 14 people had been brought in with burns. Six were transferred to a hospital in Greece.
Local residents said the army was removing ammunition, powder and shells from the depot when the blast took place but there was no immediate explanation of the cause.
Looting of military arsenals has put an estimated million weapons, from grenades to anti-tank weapons, in the hands of ordinary people.
Sporadic outbreaks of violence still happen throughout Albania, although the country is far calmer than earlier in the year.
